<!-- Source: Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman (2009), section 2.4, eq. 2.11, p. 19. -->

:::{#thm-best-predictor}
#### Conditional mean minimizes squared-error risk

Let $X$ and $Y$ be jointly distributed random variables with $\E{Y^2} < \infty$.
Let $g^*(X) \eqdef \E{Y \mid X}$.
Then for any prediction function $g(X)$ with $\E{g(X)^2} < \infty$:

$$\E{\sqf{Y - g(X)}} \ge \E{\sqf{Y - g^*(X)}}$$

with equality if and only if $\P(g(X) = g^*(X)) = 1$.
That is, the conditional expectation function $\E{Y \mid X}$
minimizes the squared-error risk among all prediction functions of $X$.

:::

::: proof

Write $Y - g(X) = \paren{Y - g^*(X)} + \paren{g^*(X) - g(X)}$.
Squaring both sides gives:

$$\sqf{Y - g(X)} = \sqf{Y - g^*(X)} + 2\paren{Y - g^*(X)}\paren{g^*(X) - g(X)} + \sqf{g^*(X) - g(X)}$$

We compute the expectation of the cross-product term by conditioning on $X$.
Because $g^*(X) - g(X)$ is a function of $X$,
by @thm-cond-pull-out it factors out of the conditional expectation:

$$
\ba
\E{\paren{Y - g^*(X)}\paren{g^*(X) - g(X)} \mid X}
&= \paren{g^*(X) - g(X)} \cd \E{Y - g^*(X) \mid X}
&& \text{(a function of } X \text{ factors out)}
\\&= \paren{g^*(X) - g(X)} \cd \paren{\E{Y \mid X} - \E{g^*(X) \mid X}}
&& \text{(linearity of conditional expectation)}
\\&= \paren{g^*(X) - g(X)} \cd \paren{g^*(X) - g^*(X)}
&& \text{(definition of } g^*(X) \text{ and } \E{g^*(X) \mid X} = g^*(X) \text{)}
\\&= 0
&& \text{(evaluate)}
\ea
$$

By the law of iterated expectations (@thm-lie),
the unconditional expectation of the cross-product is:

$$\E{\paren{Y - g^*(X)}\paren{g^*(X) - g(X)}} = \E{\E{\paren{Y - g^*(X)}\paren{g^*(X) - g(X)} \mid X}} = \E{0} = 0$$

Taking expectations on both sides of the squared expansion,
by linearity of expectation (@thm-linearity-expectation):

$$\E{\sqf{Y - g(X)}} = \E{\sqf{Y - g^*(X)}} + \E{\sqf{g^*(X) - g(X)}}$$

Since $\sqf{g^*(X) - g(X)} \ge 0$, its expectation is non-negative:

$$\E{\sqf{g^*(X) - g(X)}} \ge 0$$

with equality if and only if $\sqf{g^*(X) - g(X)} = 0$ with probability $1$,
meaning $\P(g(X) = g^*(X)) = 1$.
Therefore:

$$\E{\sqf{Y - g(X)}} \ge \E{\sqf{Y - g^*(X)}}$$

with equality if and only if $\P(g(X) = g^*(X)) = 1$.

:::

::: {.remark .notes}

The identity

$$\E{\sqf{Y - g(X)}} = \E{\sqf{Y - \E{Y \mid X}}} + \E{\sqf{\E{Y \mid X} - g(X)}}$$

decomposes the risk into two parts:

1. $\E{\sqf{Y - \E{Y \mid X}}} = \E{\Var{Y \mid X}}$,
   the expected conditional variance, which is the **irreducible risk**;
   no choice of prediction function $g(X)$ can reduce this below $\E{\Var{Y \mid X}}$.
2. $\E{\sqf{\E{Y \mid X} - g(X)}} \ge 0$,
   the **reducible risk** incurred whenever $g(X)$ differs from the conditional mean.

:::
